Retrieved 39-15-105(a)(viii)(S)(IV) allows entities occupying a data-center facility to satisfy subdivision(III) requirements in aggregate regardless of multiple ownerships of buildings and equipment. The $2 million annual-purchase threshold and $5 million/$50 million capital tiers, applicable location/retention and record conditions, and Business Council job certification still matter. The Business Council handout describes certification and Department of Revenue qualification; this is not automatic eligibility for every co-located facility.
end_condition: The retrieved Title39 compilation retains the conditional data-center exemption at 39-15-105(a)(viii)(S). SF0079/2026 Chapter19 consolidates use-tax administration into Chapter15 and repeals Chapter16 generally effective July1,2026; its section2 alone is delayed to July1,2027. The old separate use-tax section is not current code, and its repeal is not itself abolition of the data-center exemption. No sunset is stated in the reviewed data-center clause; individual eligibility, comprehensive amendment lineage, rulings and litigation remain unverified.

key_provisions: Establishes a framework and task force for covered data centers, generally facilities at 25 MW or more or meeting the referenced statutory large-load definition, subject to stated exclusions; following specified review triggers, agencies defer substantive review for not-aligned, non-performing, or non-seeking projects until required local approvals, plan consistency, and required water or wastewater authorizations are documented, and limit discretionary incentives and support, to the extent lawful; disclosure and reporting conditions apply prospectively subject to transition protections.

bill: H.5175 (194th; House text and Senate amendment S.3166)
sponsors: House energy legislation; Senate amendment S.3166
status: House engrossed H.5175 on 2026-02-26 (128-27). Senate engrossed an amended version on 2026-07-01 (32-8), reprinted as S.3166. House nonconcurred and both chambers appointed a conference committee on 2026-07-16, the latest displayed H.5175 actions in the November 9 capture; no enactment established.
key_provisions: Distinct proposed versions: House H.5175 chapter 164 section 163 defines data centers by designed load of at least 20 MW and digital-data purpose; specified new/expanded permit applicants face at least 80% renewable supply and a battery-infeasibility showing before fossil-backup permitting, alongside data-center tariffs protecting other customers. Senate S.3166 section 3 proposes data-center exemption certification conditions; sections 88 and 114 propose flexible interconnection and a working group including data-center operators. Version differences remain explicit; these are not enacted requirements.
